title: Run Lloyd's loop from a k-means++ start
brief: Write the k-means objective, the nearest-centre step, and Lloyd's loop, then seed the centres by squared distance and keep the best of several restarts.
hints: kmeans_objective: gaps = X - centers[assignments] has shape (n, d), because centers[assignments] picks one row per point. Square the gaps, add them all, and return float(...).
assign_nearest: scores = np.sum(centers**2, axis=1) - 2 * X @ centers.T has shape (n, k). Take np.argmin over axis=1. The scores can be negative, so use them only for the argmin.
lloyd: inside the loop, for each j take X[assignments == j]. Only when that group has at least one row, set centers[j] to its mean over axis 0. Then reassign and append the objective.
seeding_probabilities: divide sq_dist by its sum. When the sum is 0, every point already sits on a centre, so return np.full(n, 1 / n).

kmeans_plusplus_init: draw the first centre with rng.integers(n). For each later centre, call rng.choice(n, p=seeding_probabilities(sq_dist)), then shrink sq_dist with np.minimum against the squared distance to the new centre.
best_of_restarts: in a loop, seed with kmeans_plusplus_init(X, k, rng), run lloyd(X, k, init, 100), and keep the run whose last history entry is smallest.
